root_cause.text: ext2_iget() performed incomplete validation of ext2 inode state, accepting a corrupted inode with i_nlink == 0 but nonzero i_mode and zero i_dtime, which let an impossible ext2 inode reach VFS link-count decrement paths.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes fs/ext2/inode.c from rejecting only `i_nlink == 0 && (i_mode == 0 || i_dtime)` as deleted to rejecting all `i_nlink == 0` cases, and specifically reports `inode %lu has zero i_nlink with mode 0%o and no dtime` as corruption returning `-EFSCORRUPTED`; the CVE states this slipped-through inode later triggered `WARN_ON` in `drop_nlink()` via `ext2_unlink()`, `ext2_rename()`, and `ext2_rmdir()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: ext2_iget() performed incomplete validation of ext2 inode state, accepting a corrupted inode with i_nlink == 0 but nonzero i_mode and zero i_dtime, which let an impossible ext2 inode reach VFS link-count decrement paths.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes fs/ext2/inode.c from rejecting only `i_nlink == 0 && (i_mode == 0 || i_dtime)` as deleted to rejecting all `i_nlink == 0` cases, and specifically reports `inode %lu has zero i_nlink with mode 0%o and no dtime` as corruption returning `-EFSCORRUPTED`; the CVE states this slipped-through inode later triggered `WARN_ON` in `drop_nlink()` via `ext2_unlink()`, `ext2_rename()`, and `ext2_rmdir()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Detect and reject zero-link ext2 inodes with inconsistent deletion metadata as filesystem corruption instead of treating only some zero-link cases as deleted.
intent_record.what: The single conditional that treated an inode as deleted only when i_nlink was 0 and either i_mode was 0 or i_dtime was set was rewritten into a nested check: first testing whether inode->i_nlink == 0, then marking it deleted with ret = -ESTALE only if inode->i_mode == 0 or ei->i_dtime is set, otherwise calling ext2_error() with a corruption message and setting ret = -EFSCORRUPTED before jumping to bad_inode.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any inode with zero link count is now always rejected, but the handling is split between normal deleted inodes and inconsistent metadata. Valid deleted inodes still return -ESTALE, while zero-link inodes that still have a mode and no deletion time are now reported as filesystem corruption and return -EFSCORRUPTED instead of being silently accepted past this check.

grouping_result.intent: Detect and reject zero-link ext2 inodes with inconsistent deletion metadata as filesystem corruption instead of treating only some zero-link cases as deleted.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause in ext2_iget(): it adds validation for zero-link inodes with inconsistent deletion state (e.g., i_nlink == 0 but invalid deletion metadata), rejecting them as corruption instead of accepting them, which is exactly the missing inode-state validation described.

candidates.rationale: This conditional embodies the incomplete validation: it only rejects zero-link inodes when i_mode is zero or i_dtime is set, thereby accepting the inconsistent corrupted case of i_nlink == 0 with nonzero i_mode and zero i_dtime.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition implements the incomplete inode-state validation in ext2_iget(). It rejects zero-link inodes only when i_mode is zero or i_dtime is set, but incorrectly accepts the corrupted impossible state described in the root cause: i_nlink == 0 with nonzero i_mode and zero i_dtime.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant inode-validation logic is fully visible in `ext2_read_inode()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present in the deleted-inode check: `if (inode->i_nlink == 0 && (inode->i_mode == 0 || ei->i_dtime)) { /* this inode is deleted */ ... goto bad_inode; }`. This condition rejects only zero-link inodes when either `i_mode == 0` or `i_dtime != 0`, but it does not reject the corrupted impossible state described in the root cause: `i_nlink == 0` with nonzero `i_mode` and zero `i_dtime`. For such an inode, `(inode->i_mode == 0 || ei->i_dtime)` evaluates false, so the inode is accepted. After that, the function continues initializing the inode and even clears the in-memory deletion time with `ei->i_dtime = 0;`, allowing the bad inode to proceed into normal VFS handling. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not present in this version.
